questions.question: According to the passage, how many elements of the difference array must be changed to increase a range of values in the original array?

explanations: The passage states that for the range [3,6] in the example array, sum (3,6)=14, making 14 the correct answer.
The passage explicitly explains that the O(nlogn) bound comes from having O(logn) possible range lengths that are powers of two, leading to that many precalculated values per element.
The passage explicitly states that both functions run in O(logn) time because they access O(logn) values in the binary indexed tree, with each move taking O(1) time.
The code adds tree[a] to s only when the condition a%2 == 1 is true, which means a is odd.
The passage explains that to update a range in the original array, you only need to modify two positions in the difference array (increase at the start of the range and decrease just after the end).
